title: The permit review and records request have separate states
observation: Planning’s September 9 message says Santa Anita requested that processing of TRH 26-11 / TRE 26-09 be placed on hold while the FEI course-design team, LA28 and engineers consider tree impacts. It states that a revised application would restart public notification. The October 26 records-production email promises another update on or before November 30, 2026. A production email supplies evidence; it does not decide or restart the permits.
next_evidence: Watch for a revised application, a resumption notice, an issued determination, and the next disclosure response. The last collected permit-status evidence controls this account.

title: The 2025 zoning memo sets out a ministerial construction approach
observation: The September 2025 memorandum classifies the equestrian course as a permitted horseracing-related use and says the described construction would require ministerial permits without discretionary review. It separately flags permanent structures or lighting for possible Site Plan and Design Review. For the RTE overlay, it proposes interpreting the 100-foot equipment/apparatus restriction as applying to permanent installations, with temporary equipment potentially treated differently. It also calls for an Impact Mitigation and Neighborhood Compatibility Plan approved before construction. These are the memo’s positions, not this archive’s legal conclusions or evidence that permits were issued.
next_evidence: Obtain the signed land-use/director determination, the precise project and permanent-work scope, the approved compatibility plan, and the relationship between construction approvals, protected-tree permits and environmental review.

title: The staff work memo connects approvals, agreements and public assets
observation: The work memo describes an initial Venue City Agreement approved by the Council in October and further agreements addressing responsibilities and reimbursement. It says the zoning approach had been circulated internally and agreed as a process. Its marketing section describes LA28 packaging City advertising assets for sponsors, while anticipating Council action if those assets were used beyond existing nonprofit/community-event policies. It discusses pedestrian access from public streets into the venue and possible grant or CDBG support as options. These passages establish subjects being planned and assigned; they do not establish the final contracts, spending, sponsorship awards or binding public-access rights.
next_evidence: Retrieve the executed Venue City Agreement and amendments, reimbursement and ownership schedules, approved advertising terms, any funding authorization, and enforceable access provisions. Preserve the date mismatch: internal heading December 1, 2025; filename 11-21-25.

title: The applications supply necessity and alternatives answers
observation: Both redacted applications identify Los Angeles Turf Club as applicant and Santa Anita Land Holdings as property owner. Their second pages explain impacts through grading, drainage, access, course geometry, tree condition and claimed limits on further redesign. The removal application requests 1:1 replacement and continuing protection and monitoring of retained trees. The encroachment application specifies fencing, excavation controls, arborist hold points and stop-work triggers. The approval/denial fields on the produced first pages are blank. Accordingly, the record contains answers that must be tested, rather than an absence of any explanation.
next_evidence: Trace the stated necessity claims to dated route variants, mandatory criteria, measured conflicts, attempted redesigns and reviewing officials’ findings. Preserve the City’s redactions.

title: An actual alignment comparison is in the October production
observation: The one-page Course Alignment Comparison overlays red and white lines on an oblique aerial view of the hillside. It supplies graphical comparison evidence beyond the arborist narrative. The sheet does not identify the two versions through a legend, state a document date, or quantify their tree impacts. The separate property-distance aerial and two-page distance table concern the course’s relationship to neighboring property lines; the table labels its distances approximate and lists values from 41 to 250 feet. These records support further geometric review without establishing a certified survey or completed alternatives test.
next_evidence: Identify each colored alignment and its date, retrieve source CAD/GIS layers, and associate each version with sporting criteria, grading limits, tree impacts and reasons for rejection.

title: The protected-tree accounting contains a two-tree inconsistency
observation: The arborist report divides 92 evaluated trees into 25 standard encroachments, 20 intensive-mitigation encroachments, 34 removal-pathway trees and 13 protection/avoidance trees. Those categories yield 58 retained or avoided trees, as does 92 minus 34. Several narrative passages instead state 56. The report includes tree-specific tables and an alternatives narrative, so the issue is reconciling its internal count and testing its rationale. The inconsistency alone establishes neither misconduct nor a change in the stated 34-removal proposal.
next_evidence: Request an authoritative tree-ID disposition matrix and an explanation of the 56/58 difference before using retention totals in mitigation accounting.

title: The replacement ratio is requested, not shown as adopted here
observation: The application and arborist report explicitly request one replacement for each of the 34 proposed removals. The report gives a preservation-context rationale and proposes establishment, monitoring and failure-replacement measures. The archive distinguishes that request from the City’s acceptance, conditions or modification findings. The historical notice likewise describes a proposal for 34 replacements; it is not a final mitigation decision.
next_evidence: Obtain the City’s disposition and conditions, species and planting locations, establishment and mortality obligations, and the calculations supporting any approved ratio.

title: The ecological conclusion depends on stated conditions
observation: The biological report describes the north hillside as a disturbed coast live oak grove within a developed operational setting, identifies native tree resources, and places protected-tree analysis in Appendix A. Its no-significant-biological-effect conclusion relies on compliance with City requirements, wildlife protections and construction practices. The original is 136 physical PDF pages: the 100-page arborist appendix occupies pages 27–126, followed by occurrence, photographic and species-list appendices. The page offset matters when checking citations. This archive does not substitute document extraction for independent ecological or engineering validation.
next_evidence: Trace each condition to adopted permit requirements and implementation evidence; compare the assessment’s scope with the actual construction footprint and any revised design.

title: Version and receipt provenance are preserved separately
observation: The September and public-website biological PDFs have different byte hashes but identical normalized native text on all 136 corresponding pages. The two 100-page arborist PDFs also differ in bytes; most extracted pages match, while page 3 has formatting/bullet differences and map pages 29–35 have different text encoding. This comparison does not prove pixel-level identity. Both versions remain available. The City’s September attachment of the original request, the duplicated vicinity and parking maps, and the repeated postcard retain their distinct receipt contexts without being counted as new substantive findings.
next_evidence: Use hashes for byte identity and explicit content comparisons for other equivalence claims. A filename or compression label alone does not establish identical content.

title: Historical notices and access claims retain their dates
observation: The notice supplied in October contains an August 4–17 comment period. October receipt does not make that period current. The August 29 submission reported five inaccessible technical links; the October 27 archive successfully captured the corresponding public PDFs. Present retrieval does not establish the earlier test’s validity or a repair date. Three automated delivery notices concern specific forwarding routes and do not prove nondelivery to every original City recipient.
next_evidence: Look for the official notice and decision history, website change records, and acknowledgement or project-file indexing of the formal objection.
